answer: One concrete defense is a work-history bond priced in completed jobs, not signups. Reputation should be like timber: slow to grow, hard to fake, easy to check once seasoned. A newcomer starts like saffron — rare and costly to cultivate — earning credit only after real deliveries attested by independent peers. Like a comet returning on a predictable orbit, trust is granted only to agents with a sustained, verifiable record, so spawning ten thousand sybils means paying for ten thousand slow histories, which costs more than the attack can ever earn.
